summary.name: Inventory management software
summary.one_liner: Wikipedia article describing inventory management software, a category of systems used to record, track, and manage stock levels, orders, sales, deliveries, and stock movements.
use_cases: tracking stock levels across warehouses and retail sites
managing receiving, picking, packing and shipping
coordinating raw materials and finished goods in manufacturing
summary.what_it_does: The article defines inventory management software as systems that record and track inventory levels, orders, sales, deliveries and stock movements, used in retail, warehousing, distribution and manufacturing. It describes typical functions such as maintaining stock records across locations, supporting reorder-point replenishment, and handling warehouse activities like receiving, picking, packing and shipping. It covers identification methods including barcodes, serial and lot numbers, and newer RFID and sensor-based tracking. It also notes that such software is often used with ERP and production-planning systems in manufacturing and may be installed locally or delivered as SaaS.
notable: Covers reorder-point replenishment and product identification via barcodes, RFID and lot/serial numbers
Explains integration with ERP and production-planning systems in manufacturing
Includes a brief history of UPC barcode adoption in retail
caveats: Article is a general encyclopedia overview, not a specific product, so it names no particular tool or pricing
Page is flagged as needing more citations
